articles.title: Employment, freedom and democracy: the triple chasm between Spain and Morocco that encourages youth immigration
articles.excerpt: The two neighboring countries maintain constant geopolitical tensions stemming largely from the difference in prosperity and their political systems.
articles.author: javier-collado
articles.imageCaption: A border fence separating the two countries | EP
content: The gap in employment opportunities, personal freedoms and democratic participation between Spain and Morocco continues to drive youth migration across the strait, according to researchers who study the region.

Analysts point to three converging factors: a stark difference in youth unemployment rates, restrictions on civil and political freedoms, and limited channels for legal migration that push many toward irregular routes instead.
Both governments have periodically discussed joint economic initiatives aimed at narrowing the gap, though implementation has been slow and inconsistent.

articles.title: A Spanish NATO F-18 fighter jet shoots down a drone that violated Romanian airspace
articles.excerpt: The drone, which originated in Moldova, was detected by radar entering Romanian airspace north of the city of Galati.
articles.author: javier-collado
articles.imageCaption: NATO F-18 fighter jets on a joint patrol | EP
content: A Spanish F-18 fighter jet operating under NATO command shot down a drone that had violated Romanian airspace early Thursday morning, alliance officials confirmed.
The drone, which originated in Moldova, was detected by radar at 04:44 local time entering Romanian airspace roughly 24 kilometres north of the city of Galati.
NATO said the incident underscores the alliance's continued vigilance along its eastern flank amid ongoing regional tensions.

articles.title: The Taliban mark five years in power in Afghanistan: they ask for world support amidst 'gender apartheid'
articles.excerpt: Kabul celebrates the anniversary of the "victory" while the regime consolidates a system of exclusion that erases women from the public sphere.
articles.author: javier-collado
articles.imageCaption: A gathering marking the anniversary in Kabul | EP
content: The Taliban marked five years in power this week with public celebrations in Kabul, even as human rights groups renewed calls for international pressure over what they describe as a system of gender apartheid.
Restrictions on women's education, employment and movement have deepened steadily since the takeover, with UN officials warning the exclusion is now near total in several provinces.
Taliban representatives used the anniversary to appeal for broader international recognition and economic engagement, arguing that isolation has done little to change their approach.

articles.title: Karoline Leavitt and the work of the bloodthirsty
articles.excerpt: As Trump's press secretary, she has shown that she doesn't care at all about lying, that she despises reality, and that she hates and persecutes journalists who are not subservient to her.
articles.author: javier-collado
articles.imageCaption: A White House press briefing | EP
content: The current press secretary has built a reputation over the past year for combative daily briefings that frequently blur the line between advocacy and factual reporting, according to correspondents who cover the briefing room regularly.

Press freedom advocates have documented a pattern of hostile exchanges directed at reporters seen as unsympathetic to the administration, along with repeated refusals to correct statements later shown to be false.
Supporters counter that the approach reflects a deliberate strategy to bypass traditional media gatekeeping in favour of direct communication with the public.
